tool.name: ChIPseeker
tool.description: for ChIP peak annotation and visualization
tool.version_command: echo $(R --version | grep version | grep -v GNU)", ChIPseeker version" $(R --vanilla --slave -e "library(ChIPseeker); cat(sessionInfo()\$otherPkgs\$ChIPseeker\$Version)" 2> /dev/null | grep -v -i "WARNING: ")", optparse version" $(R --vanilla --slave -e "library(optparse); cat(sessionInfo()\$otherPkgs\$optparse\$Version)" 2> /dev/null | grep -v -i "WARNING: ")
tool.command:
#set gtf = "refgtf" #if $gtf_source.gtf_source_select == "history": ln -s '${gtf_source.gtf_hist}' $gtf && #else if $gtf_source.gtf_source_select == "cached": ln -s '${gtf_source.gtf_builtin.fields.path}' $gtf && #end if
#if $rscript: ## The R script itself lives in the (shared, read-only) tool directory, ## so it is duplicated into the output file rather than moved. cat '$__tool_directory__/chipseeker.R' > '$out_rscript' && #end if
Rscript '$__tool_directory__/chipseeker.R'
-i '$peaks' -H $header -G '$gtf' -u $adv.upstream -d $adv.downstream
#if $adv.flankgeneinfo: -F $adv.flankgeneinfo #end if
-D $adv.flankgenedist
#if $adv.ignoreUpstream: -j $adv.ignoreUpstream #end if
#if $adv.ignoreDownstream: -k $adv.ignoreDownstream #end if
-f $format
#if $pdf: -p $pdf #end if
-r $rdata

param.name: peaks
param.label: Peaks file
param.help: A peaks file in BED format.

param.name: header
param.label: Peaks file has header?
param.help: If this option is set to Yes, the tool will assume that the peak file has column headers in the first row. Default: No

param.name: gtf_source_select
param.label: Annotation source
param.help: Select a GTF to use for annotation source.

param.name: gtf_builtin
param.label: Select a built-in GTF
param.help: If the GTF file for your transcriptome of interest is not listed, contact your Galaxy administrator

param.name: rscript
param.label: Output Rscript?
param.help: If this option is set to Yes, the Rscript used to annotate the IDs will be provided as a text file in the output. Default: No

param.name: rdata
param.label: Output RData file?
param.help: Output all the data used by R to construct the tables and plots, can be loaded into R. Default: No

param.name: upstream
param.label: TSS upstream region
param.help: User can define TSS (transcription start site) region, by default TSS is defined from -3kb to +3kb.

param.name: downstream
param.label: TSS downstream region
param.help: User can define TSS (transcription start site) region, by default TSS is defined from -3kb to +3kb.

param.name: flankgeneinfo
param.label: Add flanking gene information?
param.help: If specified all genes within the flanking gene distance are reported for each peak. Default: No.

param.name: flankgenedist
param.label: Flanking gene distance
param.help: If flanking gene info is turned on the flanking distance can be specified. Default: 5000.

param.name: ignoreUpstream
param.label: Ignore upstream?
param.help: If Yes only annotate gene at the 3’ of the peak. Default: No.

param.name: ignoreDownstream
param.label: Ignore downstream?
param.help: If Yes only annotate gene at the 5’ of the peak. Default: No.

tool.help:
# ChIPseeker
ChIPseeker is a Bioconductor package for ChIP-seq data analysis. This tool annotates peaks with the position and strand information of the nearest genes, in addition to the distance from each peak to the TSS of its nearest gene. The genomic region of the peak is reported in the annotation column. The TSS (transcription start site) region, by default defined from -3 kb to +3 kb, can be adjusted under **Advanced Options**.
Since some annotations may overlap for a peak, ChIPseeker assigns the genomic annotation using the following priority:
- Promoter - 5' UTR - 3' UTR - Exon - Intron - Downstream - Intergenic
ChIPseeker also produces plots to help visualise the overlaps in the peak annotations, for example the vennpie and upset plots. See the [ChIPseeker vignette](http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ChIPseeker/inst/doc/ChIPseeker.html) for more information.
-----
## Input
- A peaks file in BED, interval or tabular format, e.g. from MACS2 or DiffBind. BED files normally have no header row (the default); if your peak file contains column headers in the first row, enable **Peaks file has header?**. - A GTF file for annotation, either from your history or one of the built-in GTFs configured in this Galaxy instance. The GTF file must contain `gene_id` and `gene_name` attributes.
Example peaks file:
| Chrom | Start | End | Name | Score | Strand | |-------|--------|--------|----------|-------|--------| | 18 | 394599 | 396513 | DiffBind | 0 | . | | 18 | 111566 | 112005 | DiffBind | 0 | . | | 18 | 346463 | 347342 | DiffBind | 0 | . | | 18 | 399013 | 400382 | DiffBind | 0 | . | | 18 | 371109 | 372102 | DiffBind | 0 | . |
## Output
- **Annotated peaks** in interval or tabular format. In addition to the input peak columns, the annotation adds the `annotation`, `geneChr`, `geneStart`, `geneEnd`, `geneLength`, `geneStrand`, `transcriptId`, `distanceToTSS`, `geneName` and `geneId` columns. In interval format these additional columns are collapsed into a single pipe (`|`) separated **Comment** column. - **Plots** (PDF): an annotation pie chart (`plotAnnoPie`), an annotation bar chart (`plotAnnoBar`), a vennpie, an upset plot and the distribution of transcription factor-binding loci relative to the TSS (`plotDistToTSS`).
Optionally, you can also output:
- the R script used by this tool - an RData file that can be loaded into R
Example annotated output (tabular format):
| Chrom | Start | End | annotation | geneChr | geneStart | geneEnd | geneLength | geneStrand | transcriptId | distanceToTSS | geneName | geneId | |-------|--------|--------|----------------------------------------------------|---------|-----------|---------|------------|------------|-----------------|---------------|----------|-----------------| | 18 | 399013 | 400382 | Promoter (<=1kb) | 1 | 346465 | 400382 | 53918 | 2 | ENST00000400256 | 0 | COLEC12 | ENSG00000158270 | | 18 | 394599 | 396513 | Intron (ENST00000400256/ENSG00000158270, intron 1) | 1 | 346465 | 400382 | 53918 | 2 | ENST00000400256 | 3869 | COLEC12 | ENSG00000158270 |
